generatedNotes: Legends re-tiers the whole Ranger book downward. In classic (P99) Rangers get their first spells at 9 and level in blocks (9/15/22/30/39/49/50+); on Legends the same spells appear from level 1 upward with per-level granularity. Level differences between `members[].level` (Legends, authoritative) and the classic level noted in `note` are therefore expected and systematic, not per-spell errors.

Legends also re-scales magnitudes: heals, DoTs and DD are markedly stronger than classic (e.g. Healing 135-175 vs classic 84-100; Stinging Swarm 27-42/tick vs classic 13/tick; Immolate 42-67/tick vs classic 24/tick), while AC on the coat line is slightly lower than classic.

Observed data-shape tell in the input file: effect strings phrased 'Increase Armor Class by N' carry Legends-tuned (usually lower) AC, while 'Increase AC by N' rows reproduce the classic P99 numbers verbatim. Every Skin-line spell appears TWICE in the file, once in each phrasing. See skin-line notes and openQuestions.

Stacking model used throughout: P99 Buff Lines groups every buff by the effect slot it writes to. 'Buffs under the same heading can't be stacked together.' Cross-line conflicts below are derived from shared headings/slots on that page.

members.name: Skin Like Nature
members.note: Classic row: Druid 49 / Ranger 59, AC 16, max HP 248-250, +2 HP/tick. Top of the Ranger chain.

replacement.note: Later members overwrite earlier ones (all write AC slot 1 and the HP Primary 'AC and HP' column, so only one can be up). BUT the chain is not monotonic in HP: Skin Like Rock scales to 105 max HP at L65 while Skin Like Steel caps at 100 max HP at L50. Above ~L50 a Ranger trades 5 max HP for 3-4 AC by moving from Rock to Steel. This quirk is classic and Legends reproduces it verbatim in both rows. Skin Like Diamond (200 HP) and Nature (250 HP) are unambiguous upgrades.

conflicts.detail: Courage, Center, Daring, Bravery, Valor, Resolution, Heroism and Fortitude all sit in AC slot 1 and in the same HP-Primary 'AC and HP' column as the Skin line. A cleric's Valor/Resolution/Heroism overwrites Skin Like Diamond/Nature and vice versa - only one lands.

Aegolism (Cleric 60) is the AC slot 1 & 4 combination buff: it blocks the Skin line AND the Aegis line at once. Per the page's own rule, a combination buff does not stack with the buffs listed underneath it.
Protection of the Glades (Druid 60, +24 AC / +470 HP) is the top of the same AC slot 1 / HP-Primary column. It overwrites any Skin-line buff on the Ranger.
Natureskin (Druid 57, +19 AC / +400 HP / +4 regen) is the Druid-only successor in the same slot; it replaces Skin Like Nature and also collides with Skin Like Nature's +2 regen in HP-Regen slot 4.
Inner Fire (Shaman 1, +3 AC / +20 HP) is in AC slot 1 - same line, blocked by any Skin buff.
Armor of Protection (Cleric 34) appears in the HP-Primary 'AC and HP' column (+225 HP), so it collides with the Skin line on HP even though its AC lives in slot 2.

Only for Skin Like Nature: its +2 HP/tick is HP-Regeneration slot 4, shared with Natureskin (+4) and the Rejuvenation potions (+10/+20/+40). A Rejuvenation potion will block or be blocked by Skin Like Nature's regen component.

stacksWith.detail: The Cleric Symbol line (Transal -> Ryltan -> Pinzarn -> Naltron -> Marzin, plus Naltron's Mark) is the separate 'HP Only and Requires Gem' column of HP (Primary). Per the page's column rule the two columns stack: Skin Like Nature + Symbol of Marzin both land. This is the standard Ranger buff pairing. Note the shared blocker: Aegolism combines both columns and therefore blocks both.
Cleric Holy Armor -> Guard -> Armor of Faith -> Shield of Words -> Aegis (and Bulwark of Faith) are AC slot 4; the Skin line is AC slot 1. They stack. Only Aegolism (slot 1 & 4) breaks this.

Shaman Talisman of Tnarg/Altuna/Kragg and the caster Shielding line are the separate 'HP (Shielding / Talisman)' heading; they stack with Skin-line HP. Focus of Spirit (Shaman 60) is explicitly exempted from the combination-blocking rule on that page.
Thistlecoat/Barbcoat/Bramblecoat/Spikecoat/Thorncoat are AC slot 2 - stack with the Skin line.
Riftwind's Protection / Call of Earth are AC slot 3 - stack with the Skin line.
Strength of Nature's +75 max HP is the 'HP (Strength)' heading, separate from HP (Primary) - it stacks with Skin-line HP. See the caveat in atk-self-line about its stacking block.

stacking.notes: The Ranger's ceiling stack is Skin Like Nature (AC1/HP) + Symbol of Marzin (HP) + Aegis/Bulwark (AC4) + a coat (AC2) + Call of Earth (AC3) + a Talisman/Shielding (HP). Accepting a cleric Heroism or an Aegolism replaces the Skin buff rather than adding to it.

While it is up, incoming buffs whose slot 4 is a max-HP increase below 400 are refused. That covers Skin Like Nature (250), Skin Like Diamond (200), Valor (200), Resolution (250) and the lower Symbols. Cast the HP buffs FIRST, then Strength of Nature. members.note: Classic Druid 29 / Ranger 49. -10 to -18 AC plus a large fire DoT. Legends 42-67/tick vs classic 24/tick.

conflicts.detail: The AC-reduction component shares a debuff slot with other AC debuffs; a stronger AC debuff on the same mob replaces a weaker one. Both members of this line carry it, so Flame Lick on an Immolated mob is a downgrade.

conflicts.detail: Members of this line overwrite each other on a target; a second Ranger casting a lower member wipes the higher one.

stacksWith.detail: Different DoT family - Immolate and Drones of Doom run together.

stacking.notes: These DoTs draw aggro on landing and each tick; the classic Ranger root-rot pattern is root + Immolate + Drones.

unlinked.info: MISSING ON LEGENDS - Chloroplast. Classic Ranger 55 (also Druid 44, Shaman 39): +10 HP/tick regeneration, HP-Regeneration slot 1. Its absence means the Legends Ranger has NO regeneration buff at all except the incidental +2/tick rider on Skin Like Nature (which is regen slot 4, not slot 1). This is the single largest capability gap versus the classic Ranger.
MISSING ON LEGENDS - Nullify Magic. Classic Ranger 58 (Kunark), Cancel Magic (4). Leaves the Legends Ranger with only the level-30 single-attempt Cancel Magic.

HP-Regeneration slot 1 (Chloroplast, Regeneration, Regrowth, Regrowth of the Grove, Fungal Regrowth) is a separate heading from HP-Regeneration slot 4 (Skin Like Nature's +2, Natureskin's +4, the Rejuvenation potions). So a Fungi Staff or a druid's Regrowth stacks with Skin Like Nature's regen rider, but a Rejuvenation potion does not.

P99 internal inconsistency worth recording: the Ranger/Spells page omits Spikecoat from its level 49 block, but the Buff Lines page lists 'Spikecoat (Self-only: Druid 39, Ranger 49)' in both AC slot 2 and Damage Shield slot 3. Spikecoat IS a classic Ranger spell; Legends has it at 42.
P99 internal inconsistency: Endure Cold and Resist Cold are listed as Ranger 22 and Ranger 55 (Velious era) on Ranger/Spells but as Ranger 9 and Ranger 49 on Buff Lines. Legends uses 18 and 55.

Classic applies a hybrid-class penalty to some Ranger casts - P99 records Greater Healing as '288 (L24) to 300 (L30) (Hybrid Classes: 244 to 270 HP)'. This is the most likely explanation for the paired Skin-line rows in the Legends file, where one row carries lower AC than the other.
Rangers have no haste spell in any era, so the shaman/enchanter Haste (Primary) line and the Ervaj/v2 line never conflict with anything a Ranger casts.

Aegolism (Cleric 60) is the only buff that occupies AC slot 1 AND slot 4 simultaneously; it therefore blocks the Ranger's Skin line and the cleric Aegis line at once, and per the P99 max-HP table it is a net -70 HP versus the best mixed stack. A Ranger being buffed by a full cleric should prefer Heroism + Aegis + Symbol over Aegolism where the choice exists.

openQuestions: Every Skin-line spell appears TWICE in the Legends file - once with 'Increase Armor Class by N' (lower AC, level equal or 1-2 lower, targetType 'Single Friendly (or Self)') and once with 'Increase AC by N' (exactly the classic P99 values and the classic Ranger level, targetType 'Single'). Are these two distinct castable spells on Legends, a hybrid-penalty variant pair, or duplicated DB rows that should be de-duplicated before display? Same question for the AC phrasing on Riftwind's Protection, the coat line and Call of Earth.

Legends' Riftwind's Protection grants +30 AC while the level-48 Call of Earth grants only +20 AC (live EQ has 11-12 and 24-25 respectively). Is the +30 intentional, and does Call of Earth actually overwrite it in-game? If it does, the level-48 spell is an AC downgrade.

Force of Nature (L50) grants +5 damage shield and +6 HP/tick - which damage-shield slot and which regen slot? If its DS is slot 1 it conflicts with Shield of Spikes; if slot 3 it conflicts with the coat line. If its regen is slot 1 it partly replaces the missing Chloroplast.

Does casting Strength of Nature's 'Block new spell if slot 4 is effect Max Hitpoints and < 400' fire on Legends? If so, Rangers must be told to accept cleric/Skin HP buffs BEFORE self-casting Strength of Nature.
Do Spirit of the Shrew / Pack Shrew's Ultravision and Chill Sight's Ultravision overwrite each other on Legends?
Are added-melee-proc buffs (Call of Sky, Call of Fire) mutually exclusive with each other and with other proc buffs on Legends? No classic-source table covers proc buffs.
Legends' Ensnare is the same -40% as Snare (duration upgrade only). Intentional re-tier or a data error?

Our wiki mirror anchors a 'Blessing of the Page line' and a 'Shielding line'. Neither appears on the P99 AC/HP tables under those names (Shielding maps to the caster AC-slot-2 / HP-Shielding-Talisman entries). Confirm against the mirror whether Blessing of the Page shares a slot with the Skin line before publishing Ranger stacking advice.

Four spells in the file have no classic-era counterpart at all and should be confirmed as Legends-authored rather than mis-transcribed: Tangling Weeds, Hawk Eye, Harmony of Nature, Swarm of Pain (plus Nature's Precision and Force of Nature, which are named like later-era live spells).

members.name: Talisman of Tnarg
members.note: P99 classic level 34; Legends re-tiers to 32. +150 max HP classic vs 134-150 on Legends.

members.name: Talisman of Altuna
members.note: P99 classic level 44; Legends re-tiers to 40.

members.name: Talisman of Kragg
members.note: Level matches classic (Shaman 55).

members.name: Focus of Spirit
members.note: Combination buff: its HP component sits IN this line (does not stack with Talisman of Kragg), but its STR/DEX components are separate lines that DO stack with the shaman STR/DEX primary lines.

replacement.note: Strictly increasing max-HP within the line (Legends: 150 -> 250 -> 380 -> 405), and all four occupy the same buff slot, so the later member always replaces the earlier. The only nuance is Focus of Spirit: you take it over Talisman of Kragg for HP, and it additionally carries STR/DEX that Kragg does not.

conflicts.line: Shielding line (Minor/Lesser/Shielding/Major/Greater/Arch Shielding, Shield of the Magi)
conflicts.detail: P99 groups these under one heading "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" — same buff slot, so a caster self-Shielding buff and a Talisman cannot both be up. Shield of the Magi (+250 HP) sits between Talisman of Altuna and Talisman of Kragg.
Cleric 34 self-only buff is listed in the same "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" heading (+225 HP) and therefore does not stack with the Talisman line.

conflicts.line: Harnessing of Spirit / Infusion of Spirit
conflicts.detail: Harnessing of Spirit carries a max-HP component (+251 on Legends) in the same family; Allakhazam commentary reports Harnessing of Spirit overwrites Infusion of Spirit. Talisman of Kragg comments explicitly say it does not stack with "HoS".

stacksWith.line: Symbol line (Symbol of Transal -> Ryltan -> Pinzarn -> Naltron -> Marzin, Naltron's Mark)
stacksWith.detail: Different column in the P99 HP table ("Primary (HP-only)"). The maximum-HP build is Protection of the Glades + Symbol of Marzin + Focus of Spirit + Divine Strength = +1775, which requires Talisman/Focus to stack with the Symbol line.

stacksWith.line: Heroism line (Courage -> Center -> Daring -> Bravery -> Valor -> Resolution -> Heroism/Heroic Bond, Fortitude)
stacksWith.detail: Cleric AC+HP line is the "Primary (AC and HP)" column; it stacks with the Shielding/Talisman column.

stacksWith.line: Skin line (Skin Like Wood -> Rock -> Steel -> Diamond -> Nature, Natureskin, Protection of the Glades)
stacksWith.detail: Druid/Ranger line shares the Heroism column, not the Talisman column, so it stacks with Talisman.
Cleric 60 combination buff sits in the Cleric (Combination) HP column and AC slots 1&4; it stacks with the Talisman/Shielding column but replaces both the Heroism and Symbol lines.

stacksWith.line: Aegis line (Guard -> Armor of Faith -> Shield of Words -> Aegis / Bulwark of Faith)
stacksWith.detail: Cleric AC slot 4 line — pure AC, no HP; unrelated slot to the Talisman HP line. NOTE: it does conflict with the shaman AC line (see ac-slot4).
Allakhazam Talisman of Kragg page lists Infusion of Spirit as stacking.

stacking.notes: This is the single most load-bearing shaman stacking fact: the Talisman line is NOT part of the cleric HP lines. A shaman Talisman + cleric Symbol + cleric/druid AC-and-HP buff all stack. What it collides with is the caster Shielding line and Cleric Armor of Protection.

unlinked.info: Buff-line stacking on P99 is expressed as numbered effect SLOTS, not as named lines. Two buffs conflict if and only if they appear under the same slot heading. This is why the shaman AC line (AC Slot 4) collides with the cleric Aegis line but not the cleric Heroism line (AC Slot 1), and why Aegolism blocks BOTH (it occupies slots 1 and 4).

The whole-game HP ceiling is +1775 = Protection of the Glades (+470, druid AC-and-HP column) + Symbol of Marzin (+700, cleric HP-only column) + Focus of Spirit (+405, shaman Talisman/Shielding column) + Divine Strength (+200, paladin column). Four different columns, one from the shaman. This single row proves the Talisman line stacks with both cleric HP lines.

The shaman strength ceiling is +240 = Maniacal Strength (+68) + Focus of Spirit (+67) + Voice of the Berserker (+85) + Primal Essence (+20). Shamans cannot use bard Anthem songs on themselves for the Anthem column, which is why their max is 43 lower than a bard's +313.

Focus of Spirit is the ONLY spell P99 exempts from its own combination rule: "If a buff (except Focus of Spirit) combines multiple lines they will be listed below it in separate columns. The combination buffs won't stack with the buffs underneath." Focus of Spirit's HP does not stack with the Talisman line, but its STR and DEX are treated as separate lines that DO stack with the shaman stat buffs.

Cross-class regen: shaman Regeneration/Chloroplast/Regrowth are literally the same spells the druid gets (at different levels), all in HP Regeneration Slot 1. A Fungi Covered Great Staff click (+15) ties Regrowth, so in the classic era the fungi staff made shaman regen redundant on anyone who owned one.
Item-worn regeneration stacks with spell regeneration but has its own combined cap of +15 HP/tick across all worn sources.
Enchanter Tashan-line resist debuffs are unresistible and stack with the shaman Malo line; the canonical raid order is Tashan, then Malo (unresistible), then Malosini (resistible, larger).
Bard songs count against the same 15-buff limit as spells, so a shaman group-buffing into a bard group can push useful buffs off.

P99 Healing Spell Lines notes that Inner Fire is more mana-efficient per HP than Minor Healing, Light Healing, Healing OR Greater Healing — the shaman "buff heal" beats their own direct heals for a long stretch of levels.
Quiescence is the post-classic continuation of the Torpor line and, unlike Stoicism and Torpor, carries no snare or slow rider. It is absent from the Legends list.

openQuestions: Legends re-tiers roughly two thirds of the shaman book downward by 1-5 levels versus P99 classic (e.g. Talisman of Tnarg 34->32, Talisman of Altuna 44->40, Superior Healing 51->45, Cannibalize 34->23). The Talisman/Kragg, Deliriously Nimble, Talisman of the Cat/Brute/Rhino/Serpent/Raptor, Regrowth, Stoicism, Torpor and Celerity levels match classic exactly. Is the downward shift a deliberate levelling-curve change, or does it need auditing spell by spell?

Is the snare-HoT line (Snails / Tortoises / Slugs / Sloths Healing) confirmed Legends-custom? The Legends patch notes call Snails, Slugs and Sloths Healing new shaman spells and "alternatives to Rancor and Stoicism", but Tortoises Healing is not named in the notes I could reach, and gnollguard.com returned 403 to direct fetching.

Are Impassivity (16) and Nonchalance (30) real EQ spells or Legends-added lower tiers of the Torpor line? Stoicism (44) and Torpor (60) are both verified classic at exactly those levels, which makes two new tiers underneath look like a deliberate Legends addition.
Talisman of the Beast (level 8, GROUP +10 STR) appears in no classic source. Is it a Legends-added group Strengthen?
Insidious Decay (52) shows a WEAKER disease-resist debuff on Legends (-36 to -42) than Insidious Malady (38) does (-49 to -60). On live EQ the ordering is reversed. Data bug or deliberate re-tune?
Remove Curse (38) removes the same 4 curse counters as Remove Lesser Curse (24) in the Legends data. Probable magnitude bug.
Instill (33) has NO effects array in the Legends file. Allakhazam confirms it is a root-line spell of roughly double Root's duration; the effect data appears to be missing entirely.
Odium (43) lists only "Increase Curse Counter by 8" with no damage component, while Curse (34) does 148/tick. Is the DoT effect missing from the record?

The file contains three duplicate/near-duplicate records: Burst of Flame appears twice identically at level 1; Invisibility versus Animals appears twice at level 10 differing only in capitalisation and duration text; Turgur's Insects appears twice at level 51 differing only in the apostrophe character. These are 3 of the 209 rows and should probably be de-duplicated in the database.
Mass Imbue Sapphire is absent while the other four gems have both single and Mass variants, and Mass Imbue Ivory's effect string wrongly reads "Summon Item: Imbued Amber".
Spirit of Cheetah is a DRUID 60 self-only spell on P99 (+115%, 8 ticks). Legends gives it to Shaman at level 21 at +75%. Deliberate class re-assignment or a class-flag error?
Sloths Healing has targetType "Single" where the other three snare-HoTs are "Target Group Member or Self" — likely a target-type inconsistency.
Avatar and Primal Avatar are identical on Legends and both castable at 60. On classic EQ, Primal Avatar is the proc from Primal Velium Weapons rather than a second castable spell.

Does Infusion of Spirit's +45 STA share the buff slot with the shaman Stamina line? Community commentary implies it does ("HoS along with Stamina beats IoS"), but I found no primary slot-level source.

Confirm whether Spirit of Bih`Li (36) and Spirit of Scale (52) occupy the same movement-speed slot as Spirit of Wolf on Legends. Neither appears on the P99 buff-lines speed table, so the conflict is inferred from the fact that all movement speed is one slot in classic EQ.

unlinked.info: Buff-slot model that drives every stacking answer above: HP/AC buffs are grouped into columns - 'Primary (AC and HP)' = Courage/Heroism + Skin + Inner Fire + Protection of the Glades; 'Primary (HP-only, requires gem)' = Symbol line; 'Shielding / Talisman' = Shaman Talisman + int-caster Shielding + Armor of Protection; 'HP (Strength)' = Divine Vigor/Glory/Strength + Ranger Strength of Nature. Buffs under the same heading cannot stack; combination buffs (Aegolism) block every column they combine.

AC is slotted separately from HP: AC slot 1 = Courage/Heroism + Skin lines; AC slot 2 = Yaulp + int-caster Shielding + druid/ranger coat line + Armor of Protection; AC slot 3 = Call of Earth, Augment/Augmentation, Frenzy; AC slot 4 = Aegis line (incl. Spirit Armor) + Shaman Guardian line + Enchanter Shield line + Magician Phantom line. A Paladin can therefore run Courage-line AC and Aegis-line AC and Yaulp AC simultaneously - three separate AC slots.

Aegolism's implementation is a hard block, not a comparison: 'Block new spell if slot 3 is effect Max Hitpoints and < 1100'. That is why an Aegolism'd target refuses Symbol buffs and Protection of the Glades.

'Blessing of the Page' / 'Blessing of the Squire' (named in the anchor set) are not Paladin spells - on Legends they are Cleric spells (Blessing of the Squire = Cleric 16, a heal-proc buff). No member of that line appears in the Paladin file, so it is not tagged here.

Live-era Paladin spells inside Legends' level range that are absent from the Legends Paladin list and whose line membership could not be verified: Salve (1), Light of Life (52), Force of Akera (53), Quellious' Word of Tranquility (54), Austerity (55, described as an HP and AC buff - probably a Courage-line member between Valor and Resolution), Holy Aura (55), Breath of Tunare (56), Guard of Piety (56), Blessing of Austerity (58).

Paladin disciplines on live (Resistant 51, Fearless 54, Holyforge 55, Deflection 59, Sanctification 60) are not spells and are correctly absent from a spell table; noted only so their absence is not mistaken for a gap.

Level offsets: Legends' Paladin levels match the live Allakhazam Paladin list almost exactly (Cease 7, Desist 13, Reanimation 22, Divine Vigor 35, Wave of Life 39, Valor of Marr 44, Thunder of Karana 47, Brell's Steadfast Aegis 49, Instill 54, Improved Invis to Undead 63), NOT the P99 classic list, which is 2-9 levels later on almost every shared spell. Legends is best modelled as the post-classic Paladin list truncated near 63.

General rule for Paladins buffing in a mixed group: cast Symbol (HP-only slot) and Aegis-line AC freely; do not cast Courage-line buffs over a Druid/Ranger Skin buff or a Shaman's Inner Fire, and never over Protection of the Glades or Aegolism.

openQuestions: Brell's Steadfast Aegis (49): does it share the HP (Strength) slot with Divine Vigor/Glory/Strength? Allakhazam's description calls it 'a group spell along the same lines as Divine Glory', which implies a conflict, but no slot-level source confirms it. If they do conflict, a Paladin cannot run Brell's + Divine Strength together and the Legends buff advice changes materially.

Divine Favor (55): the P99 Buff Lines Damage Absorption table omits it entirely, so it is unknown whether it shares the Rune/skin absorb slot with Enchanter Rune I-V and Necromancer/Wizard skin absorbs.

Reckless Strength (18) / Frenzied Strength (52): not listed on the P99 Buff Lines page; their slot relative to the Strength (Primary) line (Spirit Strength, Storm Strength, Strength) is unverified. Legends' own effect text for Reckless Strength contains player-written commentary ('Yaulp becomes better here', 'Click off before the last 40sec'), which suggests the effect string was hand-edited rather than generated.

Instrument of Nife (15) vs Divine Might (45): both are 'add melee proc' self buffs. Do they overwrite each other, and do they overwrite other classes' proc buffs? No classic source found; the one-proc-per-character assumption is inferred.

Divine Vigor (35) and Divine Glory (53) both read +100 Max HP on Legends, making Divine Glory pointless. Community reporting on the live spell puts Divine Vigor near +50. Is the Legends value intentional (a re-tier) or a data error?

Revive (39) shows no experience restoration while Reparation (31) restores 20% and Renewal (49) restores 50%. Is Revive genuinely a 0% corpse summon slotted at 39, or is the Legends effect string incomplete?
Remove Lesser Curse (34) and Remove Curse (45) both read 'Decrease Curse Counter by 4'. What actually differentiates them on Legends?
The Legends file contains two records for Invisibility versus Undead at level 17 with different casing, effects and target types. Which is canonical?
'Instill' (54) is almost certainly the classic 'Enstill' (root). Should the Legends name be treated as canonical or as a typo in the mirror? Its record also has no effects array.

Legends grants Paladins the full Cleric magic-DD line (Strike/Furor/Smite/Wrath/Retribution). Is this intentional server design, or has Cleric data leaked into the Paladin table? No classic or live source gives Paladins these spells.

Legends' Yaulp I-III are recorded as 'Permanent' duration where classic Yaulp is a short self buff. If accurate, the Yaulp upgrade order is inverted in practice (permanent Yaulp III beats a 4-tick Yaulp IV for uptime).

members.name: Heroic Bond
members.note: Group version of Heroism; identical AC/HP magnitudes on Legends. Same line - does not stack with Heroism.

members.name: Fortitude
members.note: EXCEPTION: L55 but WEAKER than L52 Heroism on Legends (AC 17-18 / HP 320-360 vs 18-19 / 360-400). Its value is duration: 2h24m vs 1h12m. p99 also lists it below Heroism (+18 AC / +345 HP vs +19 / +400).

replacement.note: Courage -> Center -> Daring -> Bravery -> Valor -> Resolution -> Heroism is strictly increasing in both AC and HP, so each replaces the previous. Two exceptions: Fortitude (55) is a lower-magnitude, double-duration sidegrade to Heroism (52), and Heroic Bond (52) is the group-cast twin of Heroism rather than an upgrade. Aegolism (60) supersedes the whole line for stacking purposes.

conflicts.detail: Verbatim p99: "These spells are cast by Clerics and Paladins to increase hit points and armor class. They do not stack with Skin line spells or Inner Fire." Confirmed structurally on Buff Lines: Courage/Center/Daring/Bravery/Valor/Resolution/Heroism/Fortitude AND Skin Like Wood/Rock/Steel/Diamond/Nature/Natureskin/Protection of the Glades all sit under the single heading "AC (Slot 1)" and in the same column of "HP (Primary)"; buffs under the same heading cannot stack.
Inner Fire (Shaman 1, +3 AC / +20 HP) shares AC Slot 1 and the HP Primary column with the Heroism line.
Protection of the Glades (Druid 60, +24 AC / +470 HP / +6 mana per tick) is the top of the Skin column in AC Slot 1 and HP Primary, so it overwrites / is blocked by Heroism-line buffs.
ONLY via Aegolism: Aegolism is the "Cleric (Combination)" entry that sits above both the Heroism/Skin column and the Symbol column, so it stacks with neither.

stacksWith.detail: Verbatim p99: Heroism-line spells "do stack with Aegis line, Symbol line, Shielding line, and Talisman line spells." On Buff Lines the Symbol line is a separate column of HP (Primary) headed "HP Only and Requires Gem (eg. Peridot)".
Heroism AC is Slot 1; Aegis-line AC is Slot 4. Different slots, they stack.
Shaman Talisman HP sits under the separate heading "HP (Shielding / Talisman)".
Caster Shielding HP is in the same separate "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" group; its AC is Slot 2.

stacking.notes: Slot map for a cleric-buffed character: AC Slot 1 = Heroism/Skin/Inner Fire; AC Slot 2 = Shielding / Yaulp / Armor of Protection; AC Slot 4 = Aegis line, shaman Guardian, enchanter Umbra. HP columns: (a) Heroism+Skin combined column, (b) Symbol column, (c) Shielding/Talisman column. Aegolism occupies AC "Slot 1 & 4" and the HP combination row simultaneously.

members.name: Naltron's Mark
members.note: Group version. EXCEPTION: caps at 446 HP vs Symbol of Naltron's 525 and Symbol of Marzin's 700 - a group convenience buff, not an upgrade.

members.name: Aegolism
members.note: p99 files Aegolism under the Symbol line, but mechanically it is the all-in-one that replaces Heroism + Symbol of Marzin + Aegis at once. Legends' own effect text carries the classic blocker: "Block new spell if slot 3 is effect 'Max Hitpoints' and < 1100" - Symbol spells put Max Hitpoints in slot 3, so Aegolism refuses them.

replacement.note: Transal -> Ryltan -> Pinzarn -> Naltron -> Marzin is strictly increasing. Naltron's Mark (58, group) is weaker than Symbol of Marzin (54, single) - buff the tank with Marzin and the group with Naltron's Mark. Aegolism (60) replaces the whole line.

conflicts.detail: All Symbol spells share the "HP Only and Requires Gem" column of HP (Primary) - only one can be up.

Aegolism blocks any incoming spell whose slot 3 is Max Hitpoints below 1100, which is exactly the Symbol line. p99: Aegolism is "an all-in-one spell, replacing Heroism, Symbol of Marzin and Aegis with a single buff with roughly the same stats and reduced overall mana cost."

stacksWith.detail: Verbatim p99: "Symbol spells increase hit points. They are cast by Clerics and Paladins. They stack with Heroism line, Talisman line and Shielding line spells."
Skin line shares the Heroism column, so the same rule applies: Symbol stacks on top of Skin Like Nature / Natureskin / Protection of the Glades. This is the key to the best classic HP stack.
Shaman Talisman HP is the "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" group - a third, independent HP column.
Symbol is HP-only; Aegis is AC Slot 4. No overlap.

stacking.notes: Symbol spells require a gem reagent (peridot etc.), which is why p99 labels the column "HP Only and Requires Gem".

members.name: Bulwark of Faith
members.note: Same level as Aegis (57) and strictly better AC (37 vs 34) but shorter duration (1h21m vs 2h24m). Both are Velious drop spells.

replacement.note: Holy Armor -> Spirit Armor -> Guard -> Armor of Faith -> Shield of Words -> Aegis is strictly increasing AC. Aegis and Bulwark of Faith are both level 57: Bulwark gives more AC, Aegis lasts longer. Aegolism (60) subsumes the line.

conflicts.detail: All seven sit under the single "AC (Slot 4)" heading on Buff Lines, alongside shaman Guardian/Shroud of the Spirits/Protect/Turtle Skin/Scale Skin/Shifting Shield, enchanter Umbra/Shadow/Shade/Obscure/Cloud/Mist/Haze and magician Phantom Armor/Plate/Chain/Leather. Only one AC Slot 4 buff can be up.
Shaman Guardian (+24) / Shroud of the Spirits (+28) share AC Slot 4 with the Aegis line - Bulwark of Faith (+37) wins.
Umbra (+29) and the Haze->Shadow chain share AC Slot 4.
Aegolism is listed under "AC (Slot 1 & 4)" - it occupies Slot 4 as well, so it blocks the Aegis line.

stacksWith.detail: Verbatim p99: "These spells are cast by Clerics and Paladins to increase armor class. They stack with Heroism line and Skin line spells."
Same verbatim statement - Aegis AC (Slot 4) layers on top of druid Skin AC (Slot 1).
Different statistic entirely.
Caster/self Shielding AC is Slot 2; Yaulp and Armor of Protection are also Slot 2.

stacking.notes: Best classic non-Aegolism AC on a tank = Bulwark of Faith (Slot 4, 37) + Protection of the Glades or Heroism (Slot 1) + a Slot 2 and Slot 3 source.

unlinked.info: THE MASTER STACKING RULE. p99 Buff Lines states it plainly: "Buffs under the same heading can't be stacked together. If a buff (except Focus of Spirit) combines multiple lines they will be listed below it in separate columns. The combination buffs won't stack with the buffs underneath, and those buffs will only stack with the other columns." Every conflict below is derived from which heading a spell appears under.

AC SLOT MAP relevant to a cleric-buffed character. Slot 1: Heroism line + druid/ranger Skin line + Protection of the Glades + Natureskin + shaman Inner Fire. Slot 2: caster Shielding line + cleric Yaulp I-IV + cleric Armor of Protection + druid/ranger coat line (Thistlecoat->Thorncoat) + magician Phantom line is actually slot 4. Slot 3: Ranger Call of Earth, enchanter Augmentation/Augment, shaman Frenzy. Slot 4: cleric Aegis line + shaman Guardian/Shroud of the Spirits + enchanter Umbra/Shadow + magician Phantom Armor. Aegolism uniquely occupies Slot 1 AND Slot 4.

HP COLUMN MAP. HP (Primary) has three parts: the combination row (Aegolism, +1100), the "AC and HP" column (Protection of the Glades +470, Heroic Bond +400, Heroism +400, Natureskin +400, Fortitude +345, Resolution +250, Skin Like Nature +250, Armor of Protection +225, Skin Like Diamond +200, Valor +200, Bravery +140, Skin Like Steel +100, Skin Like Rock +100, Center +95, Courage +20, Skin Like Wood +20, Inner Fire +20), and the "HP Only and Requires Gem" column (Symbol of Marzin +700, Symbol of Naltron +525, Naltron's Mark +446, Symbol of Pinzarn +307, Symbol of Ryltan +158, Symbol of Transal +73). A separate heading, HP (Shielding / Talisman), holds Focus of Spirit +405, Talisman of Kragg +380, Shield of the Magi +250, Talisman of Altuna +250, Armor of Protection +225, Arch Shielding +150, Talisman of Tnarg +150 and the lower Shielding spells.

THE BEST CLASSIC HP/AC STACK does NOT include Aegolism. Because Protection of the Glades (Skin/Heroism column) stacks with Symbol of Marzin (Symbol column) and with Bulwark of Faith (AC slot 4), a group with a level 60 druid and a level 57+ cleric gets 470 + 700 = 1170 HP and 24 + 37 = 61 AC plus 6 mana per tick, beating Aegolism's 1100 HP / 54 AC - and Aegolism would block PotG outright. The cleric should skip Aegolism and cast Symbol of Marzin + Bulwark of Faith on top of the druid's PotG.
Verbatim p99: "Aegolism and PotG do not stack with each other and neither will override the other." So a mis-timed Aegolism locks the group out of PotG for its full 2h30m.

Verbatim p99 on Aegolism: "For stacking purposes, this spell is considered an 'all-in-one' spell, replacing Heroism, Symbol of Marzin and Aegis with a single buff with roughly the same stats and reduced overall mana cost." And on its own page: "This buff will prevent PoTG from sticking."

The Legends Aegolism record carries the classic stacking blocker verbatim in its effects: "Stacking: Block new spell if slot 3 is effect 'Max Hitpoints' and < 1100". Symbol spells put Max Hitpoints in slot 3 (Allakhazam shows Symbol of Transal as "3: Increase Max Hitpoints"), which is the mechanism by which Aegolism refuses the Symbol line.

The DRUID SKIN LINE members, from the provided druid file and the p99 AC Slot 1 / HP Primary table: Skin Like Wood (1), Skin Like Rock (14), Skin Like Steel (24), Skin Like Diamond (36/39), Skin Like Nature (46/49), Natureskin (57), Protection of the Glades (60, group). Rangers share the line at higher levels (Skin Like Wood 9, Rock 22, Steel 39, Diamond 54, Nature 59). p99: "Druids and Rangers have access to this line of hit point and armor increasing buffs."

CLERIC vs DRUID AT COMPARABLE LEVELS (both files' own numbers, max-level values). L1 Courage 4 AC / 20 HP == Skin Like Wood 4 AC / 20 HP, tie. L7-16 Center 6 AC / 95 HP vs Skin Like Rock 7 AC / 105 HP - DRUID WINS this band. L17-23 Daring 9 AC / 130 HP vs Skin Like Rock - cleric wins. L22-31 Bravery 10 AC / 140 HP vs Skin Like Steel 10 AC / 100 HP - cleric wins. L32-41 Valor 13 AC / 200 HP vs Skin Like Diamond 13 AC / 200 HP - dead tie at cap, but the cleric gets it 4-7 levels earlier. L42-51 Resolution 16 AC / 250 HP vs Skin Like Nature 16 AC / 250 HP + 2 HP/tick - tie, druid adds regen. L52-59 Heroism 19 AC / 400 HP vs Natureskin 19 AC / 400 HP + 4 HP/tick - tie at cap, druid version arrives 5 levels later but adds regen. L60 Aegolism 54 AC / 1100 HP (single) vs Protection of the Glades 24 AC / 470 HP + 6 mana/tick (GROUP).

RESIST BUFF CEILING: the cleric line stops at +40 (Resist Fire/Cold/Poison/Disease/Magic). Druid Circle of Winter/Summer and shaman Talisman of Jasinth/Shadoo give +45 in the SAME primary slot, so a druid or shaman in group makes the cleric resist buffs redundant rather than additive.

Legends' cleric levels track the MODERN (post-revamp) Allakhazam level assignments, not the p99 classic ones. Examples: Holy Armor 1 (p99 5), Center 7 (p99 9), Daring 17 (p99 19), Bravery 22 (p99 24), Guard 25 (p99 29), Valor 32 (p99 34), Armor of Faith 35 (p99 39), Resolution 42 (p99 44), Shield of Words 45 (p99 49), Yaulp II 16 (p99 19), Yaulp III 41 (p99 44), Healing 10 (p99 14), Greater Healing 20 (p99 24), Superior Healing 30 (p99 34), Symbol of Naltron 41 (p99 44). Every one of these matches Allakhazam exactly. When annotating, use Allakhazam levels as the level authority and p99 only for line membership and stacking.

Spells present on Allakhazam's cleric list at level 60 and below but absent from Legends, beyond those noted per-line: the nine LDoN "Iony's" adventure utility spells (Lesser/normal/Greater Augury, Exorcism and Cleansing at 10/14/23/24/33/34), Epitaph of Life 52, Mark of Retribution 54, Aura of the Zealot 55, Ethereal Light 58, Blessed Armor of the Risen 58, Ethereal Remedy 59, Imbue Valor 59, Deistic Voice 59, Ancient High Priest's Bulwark 60, Ancient Gift of Aegolism 60, Blessing of Aegolism 60, Ethereal Elixir 60, Marzin's Mark 60. All are LDoN-or-later, so their absence is consistent with a classic-through-Velious spell set.

Lines with NO classic counterpart at all (Legends originals): the Echo line (Echo of Health / Echoing Light / Renewing Echo / Celestial Echo / Sacred Echo) and the Blessing of the Page proc-heal line (Page / Squire / Knight / Lord Commander). Neither name set appears on Allakhazam or p99.

openQuestions: p99 Buff Lines lists Armor of Protection's +225 HP under BOTH the Heroism/Skin column of HP (Primary) and under HP (Shielding / Talisman). Which is right decides whether a cleric self-buffing Armor of Protection loses their Heroism-line HP or their shaman Talisman HP. The Shielding/Talisman placement is more consistent with its AC Slot 2 assignment.
Armor of the Faithful (49) is on Allakhazam but on none of the p99 stacking tables, so its AC and HP slot assignments are unknown. Does it conflict with Armor of Protection, or with the Heroism line?

Legends Temperance (40) and Blessing of Temperance (45) give +800 max HP and +160 AC - values with no classic analogue at any level. Which slots do they occupy on Legends, and do they block Aegolism / PotG?
Turning of the Unnatural (37) does 25 HP/tick against Sermon of the Righteous (25) at 69-79 HP/tick. Is the Legends magnitude wrong, or are the two genuinely not one line?

Several detrimental spells quote damage at level bands far below their own spell level (Ward Summoned 17 "6 (L2) to 14 (L18)", Expulse Summoned 27 "113 (L13)", Earthquake 44 "214 (L31)", Upheaval 52 "618 (L48)", Banish Summoned 56 "529 (L43)"). Is that a scraping artefact or the real Legends scaling?
Symbol of Naltron and Naltron's Mark both carry "UNKNOWN CALC 118" in the Legends effects. p99 resolves them to +525 and +446 max HP - should those be backfilled?

Four records look like duplicates: Invisibility versus Undead / Invisibility Versus Undead (both 11), Improved Invisibility to Undead (48) / Improved Invis vs Undead (50), and two identical Imbue Emerald (29). Deduping would take the cleric list from 206 to 203.
Instill (27) and Ward of the Divine (50) have empty or stub effects arrays in the Legends data. Allakhazam gives Instill "2: Root" with a 1.1-1.6 minute duration, matching the Legends 1m36s.

Legends carries Mass Imbue Ivory and Mass Imbue Jade, which exist nowhere in the Allakhazam cleric list, and lacks Mass Imbue Emerald and Mass Imbue Sapphire, which do. Deliberate server change or data error?
The p99 Buff Lines page has no spell-haste section, so the Blessing of Piety / Blessing of Faith line has no classic stacking statement. Does it conflict with any other haste-type buff on Legends?

unlinked.info: P99 Buff Lines carries an explicit warning that the page is incomplete for item-based buffs and for "+0 rows" (buffs that block a line without contributing to the stat). Legacy of Spike, Spirit of Scale, Pack Spirit, Pack Shrew and Spirit of the Shrew have no row on it.
Focus of Spirit (Shaman 60) and Mortal Deftness stack by developer accident only if Mortal Deftness is cast first - the page flags this as the one documented exception to the slot model.
Worn HP regeneration (Fungus Covered Scale Tunic, Aura of Battle items) stacks with spell regen but has a combined 15 hp/tick cap of its own.

Live Protection of the Glades carries hard-coded stacking blocks in its spell data ("Block new spell if slot 1 is effect AC and < 108", "... slot 2 Max Hitpoints and < 2486"), i.e. it refuses to be overwritten by weaker AC/HP buffs rather than relying purely on slot identity.
P99 flags Calefaction (Druid 44) as a trap purchase: ~80pp for barely more damage than casting Firestrike twice.

Live-only druid spells with no Legends counterpart that are not Luclin+ destination ports: Healing Water (DRU/34), Spirit of Ash (DRU/36), Spirit of Eagle (DRU/54), Tangle (DRU/50), Reebo's Augury/Cleansing/Exorcism line (DRU/11-34), Mass Imbue Emerald (DRU/29), Greater Mass Imbue Emerald and Greater Mass Imbue Plains Pebble (DRU/44), Eradicate Curse/Disease/Poison and Remove Greater Curse (DRU/54-58).

openQuestions: Legends has TWO rows for Skin Like Wood/Rock/Steel and for Shield of Thorns, and two differently-levelled rows for Skin Like Diamond (36/39), Skin Like Nature (46/49), Greater Healing (29/34), Invisibility versus Animals (8/9) and Improved Superior Camo/Camou (48/50). Are these genuinely two castable spells on the server, or duplicate scrape rows for one spell? The Diamond/Nature/Camo pairs look like a live-level row plus a classic-level row of the same spell.

Ring of South Ro appears twice: level 20 (teleports to South Ro) and level 25 (Group, but the coordinates are Butcherblock -2135,1984,3). The level-25 row is almost certainly a mislabelled Circle/Ring of Butcher. Needs a server-side check.
Protection of Wood on Legends prints "+10 to +15 AC", far above live (AC 3 at L9) and above its own single-target twin Skin Like Wood (AC 2-4). Likely a data error in the Legends description.

Legends Chloroplast scales to 16 hp/tick (L50) while Regrowth is a flat 15 hp/tick, inverting the classic strict upgrade (P99 lists Chloroplast at +10, Regrowth at +15). Same for Pack Chloroplast (16) vs Regrowth of the Grove (15). Is this intentional Legends re-tuning?

The Budding/Sprouting/Flowering/Blooming/Blossoming/Efflorescing Heal line has no classic or live counterpart at all - it is Legends-custom. Which buff slot (if any) does its hp/tick occupy, and does it stack with Regrowth?

Spirit of Oak grants +4 mana/tick on Legends but appears nowhere in the P99 mana-regeneration table (only in HP Regeneration Slot 3 & 6). Which mana-regen column does it use - does it block Clarity or Mask of the Hunter?

Legacy of Spike (49) is absent from the P99 Buff Lines page; its Damage Shield (Slot 1) placement here is inferred from Legacy of Thorn and from the identical +24 magnitude it shares with Shield of Thorns.

members.note: +2 mana/tick, single target

replacement.note: Magnitude is strict (2 -> 7 -> 9 -> 11 -> 11) but targeting is NOT, so lower ranks stay in the book. Boon of the Clear Mind (group, +9) is worse per-person than Clarity II (single, +11), so a L54-58 enchanter alternates: C2 on the casters who matter, BoCM on the group. Gift of Pure Thought finally makes the group version equal to the single version and retires both. Breeze survives only as the level-14-to-26 stopgap. NOTE the Legends retier: Boon of the Clear Mind at 42 instead of the classic 52 hands enchanters group mana regen ten levels early - the largest gameplay-affecting level difference in the class.

conflicts.detail: Breeze, Clarity, Boon of the Clear Mind, Clarity II and Gift of Pure Thought ALL occupy the single "Mana Regeneration (Clarity)" slot. Only one can be on a character. Casting group BoCM over someone's Clarity II strips them down to +9 - the classic raid-buff griefing accident.

stacksWith.line: Gift line (Gift of Magic / Gift of Insight / Gift of Brilliance)
stacksWith.detail: Separate slot: "Mana Regeneration (Gift)". Gift of Insight +1/tick and Gift of Brilliance +2/tick ADD on top of Clarity II. This is the enchanter stacking their own two regen buffs on one target.

stacksWith.line: Bard Cassindra's Chorus of Clarity (L32) / Cassindra's Chant of Clarity (L20)
stacksWith.detail: Separate slot: "Mana Regeneration (Chorus)". Chorus is +7 base, and because it is a burst-per-pulse rather than a duration buff a bard who manually re-pulses it every 3s delivers an effective +14/tick. Multiple bards STACK with each other on this - each extra bard pulsing adds another +14. Unaffected by instruments/Puretone.

stacksWith.line: Bard Cantata of Replenishment (L55) / Cantata of Soothing (L34)
stacksWith.detail: Separate slot: "Mana Regeneration (Cantata)". +13/tick. Stacks with Chorus AND with Clarity - one bard can run Cantata while another pulses Chorus.
Separate slot: "Mana Regeneration (Protection of the Glades)". +6/tick.

stacksWith.line: Necromancer Lich line (Dark Pact -> Demi Lich)
stacksWith.detail: Separate slot: "Mana Regeneration (Lich)", self-only, +2 to +31/tick at an HP cost. Stacks with everything above.

stacksWith.line: Self-only caster regen (Wizard/Necro Manaskin +1, Barrier of Force click +3)
stacksWith.detail: Separate slot: "Mana Regeneration (Self-Only)".

stacksWith.line: Item mana regen ("Flowing Thought" worn items)
stacksWith.detail: P99 Buff Lines gives Flowing Thought its OWN column in the mana-regen table (+8 for wizard/necro, +6 druid), separate from every spell slot, and excludes it from the spell maximum - i.e. worn FT mana regen stacks on top of Clarity, Gift, Cantata and Chorus. Meditation (the skill, +21) is likewise a separate bucket.

stacking.notes: THE MANA-REGEN ANSWER: there are seven independent mana-regen buckets - Clarity (enchanter), Gift (enchanter), Chorus (bard), Cantata (bard), Protection of the Glades (druid), Lich (necro), Self-Only, plus non-spell Meditation and worn Flowing Thought. Everything across buckets ADDS; nothing within a bucket does. P99 documents the practical ceiling for a Magician/Enchanter as +46/tick with one bard (6 PotG + 11 Clarity II + 2 Gift of Brilliance + 13 Cantata + 14 pulsed Chorus), and notes each ADDITIONAL bard pulsing Chorus adds another +14 with no cap - four extra bards is +56 more. Legends caveat: with Koadic's Endless Intellect missing, the Clarity bucket tops out at +11 (Clarity II / Gift of Pure Thought).

standalone.note: Targeted AE that tosses everything up and deals fall damage on landing. Unique mechanic with no upgrade in the enchanter book (live adds Uproar at 63). Indoors it does nothing - the toss needs headroom.

standalone.note: Teleports the pet to the caster. Does NOT work on charmed pets, which is exactly when an enchanter most wants it.

standalone.name: Bounce
standalone.note: Self-only, 40% chance to reflect a spell, 12s duration, 2 min recast. NOT CLASSIC - absent from P99; Allakhazam has it at ENC/43 (Legends matches). Its live upgrade "Reflect" (L58) is missing from Legends. Own effect slot; nothing else in the enchanter book reflects.

openQuestions: Tashina (Legends L2): the Legends DB gives it Tashan's exact magnitudes (-9 @L4 to -13 @L8), but Allakhazam gives Tashina -6 (L2) to -18 (L9) - i.e. a WEAKER floor and a HIGHER ceiling than Tashan. If Allakhazam is right, Tashina out-scales Tashan by L9 and the line order Tashina->Tashan is wrong at high level. P99 omits Tashina from the Tash table entirely (classic P99 starts at Tashan L4). Needs a direct look at the Legends spell data to decide whether the magnitude was copied from Tashan by mistake.

Legends 'Instill' (L25) vs P99 'Enstill' (L29): Allakhazam has 'Instill' at ENC/25, so Legends is following live naming. The Legends row has NO parsed effects at all - only a 1m36s duration - so the Root effect is inferred from the duration matching Enstill/Instill exactly. Worth confirming the effect list is genuinely empty in the source data rather than a parse failure.

Four duplicate rows in the input (239 rows, 235 distinct spells): 'Wind of Tashani' L55 twice (byte-identical), 'Swift Like The Wind' at both L47 (live level) and L49 (P99 classic level), 'Invisibility versus Undead'/'Invisibility Versus Undead' both at L14 with different effect encodings, and 'Illusion: Air Elemental' at both L29 (elemental) and L45 (whose illusion id is 'Imp'). The L45 Air Elemental is the only one that might be a genuinely distinct spell - it is not on Allakhazam or P99 at that level.

Ward/Guard of Alendar stacking is INFERRED, not sourced. They are LDoN adventure-point spells and appear nowhere in the P99 Buff Lines tables, so the claim that their spell-damage mitigation is a separate slot from the melee Rune line rests on the effect type (Mitigate Spell Damage vs Absorb Damage), not on a classic stacking source.

Legends is missing Koadic's Endless Intellect (live ENC/60) even though it carries the rest of the live Clarity line including Gift of Pure Thought at 59. If that is deliberate, the Clarity slot caps at +11/tick on Legends; if it is a data gap, the mana-regen ceiling changes for every caster on the server. This is the single most consequential absence found.

The DB reports Legends 'Wonderous Rapidity' (Allakhazam spells it 'Wondrous Rapidity') and 'Wind of Tishanian' (Allakhazam: 'Wind of Tashanian'). Purely cosmetic unless something keys off exact names.

Rune I-IV effect strings in the Legends DB are unparsed ('UNKNOWN CALC 111 base 27 max 55 attrib Absorb Damage'). The base/max numbers match P99 exactly, so the values are right, but a consumer of this DB cannot read them without handling calc 111-114.

replacement.note: Strictly ordered within the element - each tier summons a higher-level elemental and the old pet must be dismissed (Reclaim Energy) before the new one is summoned. Two real exceptions: (1) pet level variance - every summon rolls a level inside the spell's range, so mages re-summon until they get a max-level pet, and a max-roll from the lower tier can briefly beat a min-roll from the new tier; (2) focus items - the lesser focus items (Torch of Alna / Shovel of Ponz / Broom of Trilon / Stein of Ulissa) raise HP of pets from spell levels 4-49, and the greater focus items (Staff of Elemental Mastery: Air/Earth/Fire/Water) add +1 to the pet level roll for spell levels 46-60. Element choice is situational, not a ladder: earth/water/air/fire are sidegrades of each other at the same tier.

stacking.notes: Pet summons are not buffs and occupy no buff slot. Only one pet at a time per caster; casting a new pet spell with a pet up fails (Legends inherits the classic single-pet rule).

members.name: Wrath of the Elements

replacement.note: Strict by magnitude, but note the tick count drops from 6 to 5, so total damage rises less than the per-tick number suggests.

conflicts.detail: A DoT will not stack with another copy of the same DoT, and the two members of this line share their damage-over-time slot - only one of the two holds on a target.

stacksWith.detail: Different spell lines land in different DoT slots and stack normally (standard EQ DoT behaviour).

stacking.notes: Detrimental DoTs are outside the scope of P99 Buff_Lines, which only tabulates beneficial buffs.

members.name: Exile Summoned
members.note: P99 era: Kunark.

members.name: Banishment
members.note: P99 era: Kunark. Not a nuke - "Destroy Target": an outright kill/despawn against summoned targets, the capstone of the family rather than the next damage tier.

replacement.note: Strict by damage from Ward Summoned to Exile Summoned. Banishment breaks the pattern: it destroys the target outright instead of dealing damage, so it is a different tool (and famously fails/resists on many raid-tier summoned mobs), not a straight replacement.

members.name: Malaise
members.note: P99 level 24, spelled the same. -15 to -20 all resists.

members.name: Malisement

members.name: Malosini
members.note: P99 era: Kunark. -60 all resists with a much longer duration (18-20 min vs 11 min).

members.name: Mala
members.note: P99 era: Kunark. Only -35 all resists on Legends - LOWER than Malosi/Malosini. Kept as a fast, cheap, low-aggro debuff rather than an upgrade.

members.name: Modulating Rod
members.note: P99 classic level 44. Summons Summoned: Modulating Rod, whose click effect is "Modulation" (converts the holder's HP into mana).

replacement.note: Single tier on Legends, so nothing to replace - but flagging the classic caveat: "mod rod" tiers on live (Modulating Rod -> Rod of Mystical Transvergence and friends) are LATER expansions. Anything the Legends DB shows beyond this one spell would be custom. Note also that the rod is cast on a target ("Single Friendly (or Self)"), which is the mechanic behind mages handing rods to the whole raid.

members.name: Summon Phantom Leather
members.note: Summons a bag containing a full set of wearable summoned leather.

replacement.note: Strict by AC of the summoned set. IMPORTANT ANNOTATION: this is a different line from the Phantom Leather/Chain/Plate/Armor SELF-BUFF line despite the shared names - one summons wearable items into a bag (8 "Summon Into Bag" effects), the other is an AC Slot 4 buff. members.name: Summon Brass Choker
members.note: Jedah's Brass Choker: +2 AC/+5 HP/+5 mana, 15% chance not to consume a spell component on spells level 12 and lower.

replacement.note: Strict by focus tier - each choker carries the same focus effect at a higher spell-level cap. Not on the P99 classic list: this whole summoned-focus-jewelry family is post-Velious (focus effects arrived with Luclin), so on Legends it is inherited from live rather than from classic.

stacking.notes: Focus effects are item properties, not buffs - they hold no buff slot, but only ONE focus of a given type applies at a time (the strongest eligible item wins).

members.name: Summon Tarnished Bauble
members.note: Jolum's Tarnished Bauble: +2 AC/+5 HP/+5 mana, ear slot; the bauble line carries a ~15% mana preservation focus on direct damage.

replacement.note: Strict by focus tier. Post-Velious family (not on the P99 classic spell list).

stacking.notes: Focus effects: only the best eligible focus of a type applies; two baubles in two ear slots do not add.

replacement.note: Strict by focus tier. Post-Velious family.

members.name: Summon Wooden Bracelet
members.note: Same level as Summon Jade Bracelet - two parallel wrist items with different focus effects, not a tier pair.

replacement.note: Not strict: two level-20 bracelets exist side by side (Wooden and Jade), which is the signature of two different focus effects rather than a ladder, and the same is likely true of Opal vs Stone at 42/44. Needs per-item focus-effect confirmation before asserting an upgrade order.

stacking.notes: Focus effect items. Two wrist slots exist, so a mage can genuinely wear two of these at once - but two copies of the SAME focus type do not stack.

members.note: Highest summoned apparel piece on Legends; slot unconfirmed (back/shoulder).

standalone.note: Shared with every caster class; no mage-specific tiering.

standalone.name: Identify

standalone.note: P99 era: Velious. "Call Pet" - teleports the existing pet to the caster. No tiers.

standalone.name: Bounce
standalone.note: NOT on the P99 classic list. Live/LDoN-era spell (Magician 42, 72 adventure points, North Ro camp): +40% chance to reflect spells for 12 seconds, 2 minute recast. Legends level matches live exactly.

standalone.name: Primal Remedy
standalone.note: NOT on the P99 classic list. Legacy of Ykesha quest spell (Vera/Vira, Gunthak/Temple of Sol Ro): a pet heal-over-time (120 HP/tick for 30s) used to top the pet off between casts of the main pet heal, and lower aggro than a direct heal. standalone.name: Ward of Calliav
standalone.note: NOT on the P99 classic list. LDoN-era pet rune (mage version bought with adventure points at Mistmoore Catacombs) - pet absorbs several hits before taking damage. The Legends absorb value (11747) is far above the live classic-era value and looks re-tuned; flag for magnitude review.

standalone.name: Call of the Hero
standalone.note: P99 era: Kunark. The mage signature summon-a-player spell. Single tier, no upgrades.

standalone.name: Rage of Zomm

standalone.name: Bristlebane`s Bundle
standalone.note: P99 era: Kunark. Novelty party bundle (Summoned: Cake, Ale, Spinning Bottle, A Firework). Not an upgrade of the food/drink line - it is the joke spell, kept separate.

standalone.name: Dyzil`s Deafening Decoy
standalone.note: P99 era: Kunark. Summons a decoy pet used to pull/hold aggro. Single tier, unrelated to the elemental pet ladders.

standalone.note: P99 era: Velious. Grants the pet fear immunity for 3.5 minutes. Single tier.

standalone.name: Manastorm

openQuestions: The Legends export contains TWO identical "Burst of Flame" rows at level 1 (same effects, same type). Treated as one spell here; recommend de-duplicating the DB record.

Two rows named "Summon Orb" at level 45 and level 46. P99/classic has a single Summon Orb (classic level 44, summons Summoned: Orb of Mastery). Is the level 46 row a distinct live spell, a re-tier artifact, or a duplicate record?

Mala (60) is only -35 all resists on Legends, below Malosi (51, -59/-60) and Malosini (58, -60). On live, Mala is the lower-magnitude quick-cast member of the family. Does it occupy the same debuff slot as Malosini on Legends (i.e. overwrite it), or a separate one? Not resolvable from P99, which does not tabulate debuff slots.

Ward of Calliav on Legends absorbs "up to 11747 damage" - orders of magnitude above the classic/LDoN-era value. Either the Legends DB is showing a scaled/max-level figure or the spell has been re-tuned. Needs a magnitude check against the server data, not against web sources.

Burnout stacking with enchanter/bard haste ON A PET is inferred from the shared "Haste (Primary)" line - P99 Buff_Lines does not tabulate pet-only buffs, so this is medium confidence rather than sourced fact.

Summon Elemental Defender (11) and Summon Elemental Blanket (48) are grouped with the summoned mantles as "summoned focus apparel" on the assumption they are wearable focus items. Their equipment slots were not confirmed from a source.
Summon Wooden Bracelet and Summon Jade Bracelet are both level 20. Confirm whether they carry different focus effects (expected) before treating either as an upgrade of the other.
notes: LEVELS: Legends levels track modern/live Allakhazam, not P99 classic. P99 grants magician spells in 4-5 level tiers (1/4/8/12/16/20/24/29/34/39/44/49...), while Legends spreads them one per level. Every level difference recorded in member notes is that systematic offset, not a data error.
ERA TAGS in member notes ("P99 era: Kunark/Velious") come from the era column of the P99 Magician spell table.

MISSING FROM LEGENDS (whole-class sweep against the P99 classic-through-Velious magician list): Gaze (16), Serpent Sight (16), Enduring Breath (20), Ultravision (29), Levitation (39). Everything else on the P99 list is present on Legends. Nothing else is missing.

PRESENT ON LEGENDS BUT NOT CLASSIC (post-Velious, inherited from live rather than Legends-custom): the entire summoned focus jewelry/apparel family (chokers, baubles, rings, bracelets, mantles, Elemental Defender, Elemental Blanket), the Summon Phantom Leather/Chain/Plate armor-set summons, Summon: Orb of Exploration, Refresh Summoning, Primal Remedy (LoY quest), Bounce (LDoN), Ward of Calliav (LDoN). No spell in the Legends list is unattested on live - there are no clearly Legends-invented spells in this class.

STACKING MODEL: slot-based per P99 Buff_Lines. Buffs listed under the same heading do not stack; a spell that touches several statistics appears under several headings and blocks in each of them independently.

members.name: Dark Pact
members.note: -2 HP/tick, +2 mana/tick. P99 level 8.

members.name: Allure of Death
members.note: -5 HP/tick, +4 mana/tick. P99 level 20.

members.name: Call of Bones
members.note: -10 HP/tick, +8 mana/tick, adds bleached-skeleton illusion + ultravision. P99 level 34.

members.name: Lich
members.note: -22 HP/tick, +20 mana/tick, bloody-skeleton illusion. P99 level 49.

members.name: Arch Lich
members.note: -20 HP/tick, +20 mana/tick, spectre illusion + see invis. Velious drop. Sidegrade to Demi Lich: same mana, far cheaper HP.

members.name: Demi Lich
members.note: -48 HP/tick, +31 mana/tick. Highest mana return, highest HP cost.

replacement.note: Strictly ascending through Lich, then splits. Arch Lich (20 mana / -20 HP) and Demi Lich (31 mana / -48 HP) are a deliberate choice, not an upgrade: Arch Lich is the sustainable/low-HP-pool option, Demi Lich the max-throughput option. Lower ranks stay useful when HP regen cannot cover the drain (classic 'lich you can afford' rule), so no rank is ever obsolete in practice.

conflicts.detail: All six occupy the single 'Mana Regeneration (Lich)' line; only one can be up. Casting a different rank replaces the active one.

Call of Bones / Lich / Arch Lich / Demi Lich carry an illusion component, so they collide with any other illusion (Enchanter illusions, Form of the X, gnomework illusions) the way illusions normally do.
conflicts.source: Legends spell data (Illusion: 60 / Illusion: 85 slots) + https://wiki.project1999.com/Buff_Lines (illusions tracked separately)

stacksWith.detail: Clarity / Clarity II / Boon of the Clear Mind / Gift of Pure Thought / Breeze - separate slot, fully additive.

stacksWith.line: Mana Regeneration (Cantata / Chorus / Gift / Protection of the Glades)
stacksWith.detail: Bard Cantata of Replenishment, Cassindra's Chorus of Clarity, Enchanter Gift of Brilliance, Druid Protection of the Glades all stack with Lich.
Manaskin's +1 mana/tick is a different slot and stacks with the Lich line (P99 explicitly tables Necromancer +67 mana regen with Demi Lich + Manaskin + everything else).

The HP drain is a separate effect slot, not part of any HP-regen buff line. It does not block, and is not blocked by, Regeneration/Chloroplast/Regrowth, Hymn of Restoration, worn regen or Iksar innate regen - the values simply sum arithmetically. This is the classic 'regen offsets lich' interaction and is why the P99 Necromancer page tables Iksar-vs-non-Iksar HP regen under Lich.

stacking.notes: PRIORITY FINDING: the Lich line's HP drain and the game's HP-regeneration buff lines are independent - they net out numerically rather than overwriting each other. P99's Buff_Lines page lists Necromancer max HP regen (+129) and the Lich mana slot separately, and gives a '(Necromancer w/ Lich)' mana row of +67 that includes Demi Lich's +31 alongside every other mana-regen line. The drain is applied every tick regardless of current HP and will kill an unbuffed necro at low HP (hence Harmshield/Quivering Veil and lifetap discipline).

members.name: Clinging Darkness
members.note: 5/tick, -24% to -30% movement.

members.name: Engulfing Darkness
members.note: 11/tick, -40%. P99 level 12.

members.name: Dooming Darkness
members.note: 20/tick, -49% to -60%. P99 level 29.

members.name: Cascading Darkness
members.note: 72/tick, -60%. P99 level 49.

members.name: Devouring Darkness
members.note: 107/tick, -69% to -70%. Fewer ticks than Cascading (13 vs 16), so lower total damage - cast for the snare, not the DPM.

replacement.note: Snare magnitude and damage ascend, but Cascading Darkness (3.84 DPM, 16 ticks, 1152 total) beats Devouring Darkness (3.48 DPM, 13 ticks) on efficiency, so Cascading stays in the book at 59. Lower ranks remain the cheap fear-kite snare.

conflicts.detail: Same-line DoTs never stack with each other; a higher rank overwrites a lower, and a lower will not land over a higher.
Shadow Knights get Clinging / Engulfing / Dooming / Cascading Darkness - same line, so a necro and an SK cannot both have a Darkness DoT on the same mob in the classic/Velious ruleset.
Scythe of the Shadowed Soul's click (75/tick, 16 ticks, snare) is explicitly on the Darkness DoT line and will not stack with any Darkness spell.

stacksWith.detail: Disease, Fire, Poison, Life Drain, Muscle and Splurt all stack alongside a Darkness DoT.
Different spell lines from any class stack (shaman poison/disease, druid fire/poison, wizard, enchanter).

stacking.notes: The snare component follows the same rule as any other movement debuff - a stronger snare from another class (Ranger/Druid Ensnare, Snare) is a different line and can overwrite the movement effect independently of the DoT.

members.name: Disease Cloud
members.note: 5 initial + 1/tick for 30-60 ticks. Classic pull/aggro tool.

members.name: Infectious Cloud
members.note: Targeted AE version, 20 initial + 5/tick, 21 ticks. P99 level 16.

members.name: Scourge
members.note: 40 initial + 24/tick, 21 ticks. P99 level 39.

members.name: Plague
members.note: 60 initial + 55/tick, 22 ticks. 4.23 DPM.

replacement.note: Damage ascends strictly, but Disease Cloud is never retired (10 mana, 30-60 tick duration, best pull/aggro-tag tool in the game) and Infectious Cloud is the only AE member. All four have a direct-damage component that can break root.

conflicts.detail: Same line - Scourge overwrites Infectious Cloud, Plague overwrites Scourge, and an inferior member will not land over a superior one.
Shadow Knights share Disease Cloud, so the line collides across the two classes at the low end.

stacksWith.line: Muscle (Heart Flutter / Asystole / Cessation of Cor)
stacksWith.detail: Also disease-based but a SEPARATE line - a necro can run Plague and Cessation of Cor on the same mob simultaneously. Damage type does not determine the line; the spell line does.
Darkness, Fire, Poison, Life Drain, Splurt all stack alongside.
Different lines (e.g. shaman Affliction/Sicken line), so they stack.

stacking.notes: Long durations mean the tabled DPM is deceptively high - the P99 line table flags that these usually get clipped.

members.name: Heat Blood
members.note: 17/tick. P99 level 12.

members.name: Boil Blood
members.note: 24/tick, 16-21 ticks. P99 level 29.

members.name: Ignite Blood
members.note: 56/tick, 21 ticks, 4.7 DPM. P99 level 49.

members.name: Pyrocruor
members.note: 111/tick, 19 ticks, 5.27 DPM - the necro's most efficient non-Splurt DoT.

replacement.note: Clean ascending chain in damage, DPM and duration. All members carry a -100 fire resist modifier. Only reason to keep a lower rank is mana budget at low level.

P99's Buff_Lines page only tracks stat effects, so it lists DMF under Poison Resistance ONLY; the levitate / see-invis / water-breathing components are not slot-tabled anywhere authoritative and their interaction with other levitate/see-invis buffs is an open question.

replacement.note: NOT a replacement pair. Deadeye grants see-invisible (which Shadow Sight lacks); Shadow Sight upgrades infravision to ultravision. Both are commonly kept up, and Skin of the Shadow (55) supplies the ultravision half.

conflicts.detail: Infravision and ultravision are the same underlying night-vision effect; ultravision wins. See-invisible is separate.

stacksWith.detail: DMF also grants See Invisible(1) - redundant with Deadeye rather than additive.

stacking.notes: Not stat buffs, so untabulated on P99 Buff_Lines.

members.name: Harmshield
members.note: 3 ticks of total damage immunity, costs 20 HP on cast. Research spell. Cannot attack or cast while up.

members.name: Quivering Veil of Xarn
members.note: Same 3-tick invulnerability but HEALS 150 on cast instead of costing 20 HP, and is cheaper per second of safety. Kunark NPC drop.

replacement.note: Quivering Veil is strictly better (heal instead of cost) at the same duration. Harmshield is kept only until 58.

conflicts.detail: Only one invulnerability effect at a time; nothing else stacks meaningfully during it.

stacking.notes: The classic necro survival trick: Harmshield/QVoX to survive a Lich drain spike or a train, since damage-over-time and melee are both nullified.

members.name: Dark Empathy
members.note: Caster loses 30 HP, target gains 30. P99 level 8.

members.name: Corporeal Empathy
members.note: 215 for 215. Velious NPC drop. P99 level 44.

replacement.note: Straight magnitude upgrade of the same 1:1 HP transfer.

stacking.notes: Instant heals - no buff slot.

lines.name: Self-cost heal over time (Shadow Compact / Pact / Bond)

members.name: Shadow Compact
members.note: Target healed 20/tick for 4 ticks at the caster's HP cost. 10 mana. P99 level 20.

members.name: Pact of Shadow
members.note: 80/tick for 4 ticks (P99: caster loses 45/tick, target gains 81/tick - a net HP profit). 10 mana.

members.name: Shadowbond
members.note: 125/tick for 4 ticks. 10 mana. Quest spell (Vaean the Night).

replacement.note: Ascending throughput, identical shape and 10-mana cost throughout. The necro's mana-free group heal - HP is the resource, refilled with lifetaps.

conflicts.detail: Same line - recasting refreshes; a lower rank will not land over a higher one on the same target.

stacksWith.detail: These are heal-over-time spells, not regen buffs, and are additive with Regeneration/Chloroplast etc.

stacking.notes: The 'necro as backup healer' loop: Shadowbond the tank at 10 mana, then lifetap yourself back up. Interacts with the Lich drain - both are HP outflow at the same time.

members.name: Mend Bones

members.name: Renew Bones

members.name: Emissary of Thule
members.note: SPECTRE warrior, pet 43-47, ~2700 HP, immune to fear. Terminal member.

replacement.note: Strict pet-level ascent through Invoke Death (48). Above that the line branches by pet CLASS: Minion of Shadows (rogue/backstab, best burst on a rooted mob), Servant of Bones (monk/flying kick), Emissary of Thule (spectre warrior, most HP, fear-immune). All three plus Invoke Death stay memorised situationally. Only the Emissary is fear-immune, which matters for fear-kiting groups. The Encyclopedia Necrotheurgia focus adds +1 pet level for spells 46-60.

members.name: Focus Death
members.note: +15% attack speed, +20 STR, +2 AC. Real live spell (Allakhazam 2541, Luclin-era Echo Caverns vendor). Absent from P99 - the lowest tier the classic set does not have.

members.note: +22% to +30% attack speed, +26 to +33 STR, +6 to +8 AC. Research spell. P99 level 24.

replacement.note: Every stat ascends, but Augmentation of Death's duration drops from 60 minutes to ~17.5, so the 60-minute Augment Death is still worth casting when you will not be refreshing. Otherwise a clean chain.

conflicts.detail: A pet buffed with an enchanter/shaman haste (Alacrity, Celerity, Quickness, Swift Like The Wind) and the Death line share the primary haste slot - the stronger wins. Enchanter haste generally beats the necro's own on a pet.

stacksWith.detail: Bard Composition/Melody of Ervaj is a second haste slot and stacks.

stacking.notes: The STR and AC riders travel with the haste spell, so they are gained or lost together when a stronger haste overwrites.

members.name: Form of Chilled Bone

members.name: Sacrifice

members.name: Convergence

members.name: Levant

standalone.name: Vampiric Embrace

standalone.name: Bind Affinity
standalone.note: Sets bind point. No line.

standalone.note: The class-defining utility. No upgrade rank exists for necromancers (unlike monks' skill-based FD). Instant, 60 mana.

standalone.note: Item lore. No line.

standalone.note: Single-target mesmerise (up to level 55) + 1% memory blur, 3 ticks. The necro's only mez. No upgrade rank. Feared/mezzed targets conflict: mez and fear cannot both hold a mob.

standalone.name: Eternities Torment
standalone.note: Undead-only DoT, 30/tick for 2 min 6 s. Real live spell (Allakhazam 2543, Luclin-era Echo Caverns vendor batch alongside Focus Death and Shackle of Bone). No P99 equivalent and no other rank - an unlined undead DoT. Whether it collides with the Disease or Darkness line is unverified.

standalone.name: Dark Soul
standalone.note: Curse-counter DoT, 96-140/tick for 30 s. Real live spell (Allakhazam 4096). No P99 equivalent, no sibling ranks. Curse counters mean only a Remove Curse cures it.

standalone.name: Summon Companion
standalone.note: Calls the pet to the caster. Velious. No line.

standalone.name: Bounce
standalone.note: 40% chance to reflect a spell, 12 s. Real live spell (Allakhazam 4099), researched (Pristine Supple Runic Hide + Quill of the Arch Lich). No P99 equivalent, no other rank.

standalone.name: Insidious Retrogression
standalone.note: 546-550 damage + 10% snare + -25 STR + -25 ATK over 1 min 36 s. Real live spell (Allakhazam 2545). Described as an aggro-kite opener. Not on P99; unlined.

standalone.name: Ward of Calliav
standalone.note: Pet damage rune (Legends lists 'Absorb Hit up to 11747 damage', a suspiciously large figure). Real live spell, MAG/NEC/BST 46-49. First member of the Calliav pet-rune line.

standalone.name: Infusion
standalone.note: Restores 1000 mana to self, 1 mana cost, consumes an Essence Emerald. Kunark NPC drop. Paired with Sacrifice as the emerald consumer; no upgrade rank.

openQuestions: Dead Man Floating's non-resist components (Levitate(2), See Invisible(1), Water Breathing(2)) are not slot-tabled on any authoritative classic source - P99's Buff_Lines only tracks stat effects and lists DMF solely under Poison Resistance. Whether DMF's levitate overwrites (or is overwritten by) druid/shaman/wizard Levitate, and whether its See Invisible collides with Deadeye, needs in-game testing on Legends.

Legends' Shackle of Spirit (L38) shows -10% melee haste while Shackle of Bone (L17) shows -20%. The higher-level spell should be the stronger slow; this looks like a data error in the Legends DB rather than a design choice.
Legends' Envenomed Bolt shows 351 damage per tick vs the classic 146 per tick (and 41 initial vs 110). Either Legends re-tuned the spell or the DB row is wrong.

The 'of Life' healing-reduction DoTs (Cancelling / Negation / Cessation of Life, levels 8/18/37) have no Allakhazam counterpart. Confirmed Legends-custom with high confidence, but their stacking behaviour against the classic DoT lines is untested.

Defoliate (L29) is a Druid spell name; Allakhazam's Necromancer list returns only Defoliation (52). Legends appears to have granted necros a lower plant nuke - confirm whether it is a Legends addition or a re-tier.

Eternities Torment (L27) and Dark Soul (L39) are real live spells with no sibling ranks and no P99 data - their DoT-line membership (and therefore what they will and will not stack with) is unresolved.

The Strength-debuff slot: Siphon Strength / Wave of Enfeeblement / Surge of Enfeeblement vs the Muscle DoT line's -STR component vs shaman Cripple/Weaken. P99's Buff_Lines page covers beneficial buffs only, so no authoritative slot table exists for detrimentals.

Legends carries four duplicate rows: Leach (L9 and L12), Rapacious Subvention (L21 and L24), Invisibility versus Undead / Invisibility Versus Undead (both L1), Improved Invis vs Undead / Improved Invisibility to Undead (both L50). These are almost certainly ingest duplicates, not re-tiers; recommend collapsing.
Legends' 'Instill' (L53) is the classic 'Enstill' and its DB row has no effects array at all - it needs the root effect populated.
P99's Buff_Lines Cold Resistance section omits Necromancer from Endure Cold / Resist Cold even though the P99 Necromancer spell list grants both. Treated here as a wiki gap.

lines.name: Fire Direct Damage (Shock of Fire line)

members.name: Fire Bolt
members.note: P99 L8; Legends L5. P99 target type "Line of Sight"; Legends "Single".

members.note: P99 L16 for 102-110; Legends L15 for 145-175 - magnitude disagreement, not averaged.

members.note: P99 L44 for 590-625; Legends L43 flat 900.

members.name: Draught of Fire
members.note: Kunark efficiency nuke: far better mana/cast-time than Conflagration despite similar damage.

replacement.note: Damage rises monotonically, but the newest spell is not always the best. P99 explicitly warns "just because a spell has a bigger damage number doesn't always mean that spell is the best spell in that line." The Kunark Draughts (215 mana / 3s cast) beat the older big-ticket nukes on both mana efficiency and DPS, so Conflagration stays situational (burst) rather than being retired.

members.note: DUPLICATE DB ROWS: two "Shock of Frost" entries both at L1, one for 4-6 (matches P99) and one for 11-28. Treated as one line member; the second row is almost certainly a re-tuned/duplicate spell id on Legends.

replacement.note: Magic-resist nukes exist to bypass fire/cold-resistant mobs; the line is otherwise a clean damage ramp. Rend (280 mana, 6.3s) vs Voltaic Draught (215 mana, 3s) is the same efficiency-over-raw-damage inversion seen in the fire and cold lines.

members.note: NOT on the P99 wizard list. Legends carries a 1.00 sec/55 stun and 218-252 damage at L17, which is far above the L16 Lightning Bolt curve (130-157). Possibly Legends-custom or a live-only spell; flagged.

replacement.note: Strict within the sub-line. P99 splits these from the true stun line by the tell "Stuns with 0 second duration are intended to interrupt spell casting mobs" - these are nukes that happen to interrupt, not crowd control. P99 also warns all stun-component spells are high-aggro.

members.note: 8 sec stun, 750 damage.

members.name: Enticement of Flame
members.note: Fire. Legends 482-500; P99 360.

members.name: Lure of Frost
members.note: Cold, 640.

members.name: Lure of Flame
members.note: Fire, 640. Replaces Enticement of Flame.

members.name: Lure of Lightning
members.note: Magic, 680.

members.name: Lure of Ice
members.note: Cold, 825. Replaces Lure of Frost.

replacement.note: SITUATIONAL, NOT STRICT - the defining exception in the wizard book. Lures carry a built-in resist adjustment and are, per P99, "very hard for mobs to resist, as long as the mob is not immune to that resist type." They trade damage-per-mana against landability: at 320 mana for 640-825 damage they are strictly worse than the Draughts (215 mana for ~690) on a low-resist mob, and strictly better on a high-resist raid target. Within the line, replacement is per-element only: Lure of Ice replaces Lure of Frost (cold) and Lure of Flame replaces Enticement of Flame (fire); Lure of Lightning (magic) replaces nothing and is replaced by nothing.

members.name: Pillar of Frost
members.note: Legends spell text explicitly chains this one: "replacing Circle of Force and being replaced by Pillar of Lightning" - honored as a Legends-authored line statement.

members.name: Thunderbold
members.note: SITUATIONAL BRANCH: P99 lists it in the Quad AE table, but it carries a 3.0 sec stun and 600 flat damage. It is a stun-AE, not a damage upgrade over Pillar of Lightning (828-848) - and it is a high-aggro spell.

replacement.note: Strict along the main chain (Column of Frost -> Pillar of Fire -> Column of Lightning -> Circle of Force -> Pillar of Frost -> Pillar of Lightning -> Pillar of Flame), and Legends' own spell descriptions state the chain explicitly. Thunderbold is the one exception: it sits at the same level as Pillar of Lightning with materially less damage and is kept for its stun. Note the whole chain rotates element (cold -> fire -> magic -> magic -> cold -> magic -> fire), so an earlier member is occasionally still the right pick against an element-resistant camp.
